label: Gala — Meryl

sprite.name: Meryl Silverburgh — original MGS1
sprite.incarnation: Meryl Silverburgh of original MGS1, recognizable auburn short wavy hair, athletic young woman, determined human face, same anatomy. Original bespoke feminine evening tuxedo: fitted black dinner jacket with satin peak lapels, white collar shirt, rich burgundy silk waistcoat, small black bow tie, slim black formal trousers with satin side stripe, practical black lace-up formal combat shoes and original fingerless black gloves. Discreet thigh holster only when it exists in the pose. Her shoulder tattoo stays beneath the sleeve; do not print a tattoo on cloth. Same source handgun or equipment in the same exact hands where present. Distinct tailored shape, not a generic male suit or a recoloring of fatigues.

limits: Original costume design has no attested released canonical appearance; absolute canonical 1:1 is not claimed.
Native imagegen output bytes are preserved unchanged. Read-only source geometry is not pixel editing.
All physical pose keys, original UID/actionMap/phaseMap remain inherited; this is not original-game animation extraction.
Aiming, punches, throws, sweep, grenades, reload and KO are original2D versus adaptations; not native PS1 animation extraction or pixel-certified source clones.
Primary official Konami body artwork is painterly: colors reconciled with original emulated game captures, which are filtered/non-native aspect; not absolute PS1 pixel certification.
B-left last-column bootmargin narrow although complete and0 opaqueedge; final runtime crop/scale/pose validation belongs sequential integration owner.
Some native generator output includes very-low-alpha RGB fringes; no recoloring/alpha repair/image editing outside imagegen performed.
Tiny firearm and tattoo engravings are not certified at subpixel detail; pose handgrips are closest reviewed reference adaptation.

Standing source pixel scale is manually observed per independent PNG; low/crouch/KO preserve that scale instead of stretching to full standing height. Local display height is a versus adaptation, not a source-frame pixel certification.
Grenade action belongs to the authored CQC versus adaptation stated in the preserved original profile. Meryl scripted original PS1 grenade use is not claimed.

Very close source rows require a Canvas contour restricted to pixels closest to the selected body component; no neighboring boot fringe should be drawn over a gun pose head. The alpha PNG itself remains unchanged.
Original identity source reconstruction is inherited, not a publisher-extracted pixel-perfect animation. Vector alpha component geometry isolates whole bodies without reencoding any PNG.

Runtime clip follows read-only outer alpha16 component contours, adaptively simplified at0.25–1 source pixel with oppositely wound native alpha holes, retaining zero neighboring alpha16 pixel centres inside the path; it excludes neighboring body pixels inside an earlier convex hull. Native PNG pixels and physical source rectangles remain unchanged.

All source poses and both native directions reviewed physically in raw atlases and checkerboard Canvas captures. Standalone runtime validation completed before this option was marked verified. Source MGS1 identity reconstruction limitations remain inherited.
